summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 67 'TEE Lease-Renewer Contract Rewrite' for CipherBox, rewriting the TEE worker from a record originator into a verify-in-enclave record-lease-renewer (TEE-01/02/03/06), with integrated research, wave-based parallel execution, and a live migration + sdk-e2e round-trip gate.
summary.outcome: All 8 plans executed across 3 waves; the live migration applied and both round-trip tests passed (Test A: equal-seq/equal-CID/later-EOL; Test B: tombstone never re-signed). Two bugs surfaced by the live gate were fixed: a TypeORM query-builder `databaseName` crash in `getDueEntries` and a wrong SQL column name in the e2e suite's `readTeeKeys`. A final commit for the bug fixes timed out on the 1Password signing prompt and requires confirmation.

repo: The GSD commit helper reliably reports `commit_failed` even when the commit lands — always verify with `git log --oneline -1` before retrying; never trust the helper's status field.
`apps/api` is intentionally red between Wave 1 and Wave 2: 67-01 slims the entity, 67-07 restores callers — only the scoped tee-worker suites and sdk-core need to be green after Wave 1.

Two Postgres databases coexist locally: `cipherbox` (real dev DB, what `app.module.ts` defaults to at line 85) and `cipherbox_test` (CI DB). `apps/api/.env` had a stray `DB_DATABASE=cipherbox_test` that caused the migration CLI to target the wrong DB; must force `DB_DATABASE=cipherbox` explicitly for local migration runs.

The TEE simulator key is deterministic (HKDF from fixed seed `'cipherbox-tee-simulator-seed'`) — rebuilding the tee-worker image doesn't change the public key, so `tee_key_state` doesn't need to be reset after a rebuild.
`mock-ipns-routing` permanently occupies `127.0.0.1:3001`; any local tee-worker service must map to `:3002:3001` with `TEE_WORKER_URL=http://localhost:3002`.

The `apps/tee-worker/Dockerfile` COPYs `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and `packages/*` from the monorepo root, so the docker-compose `context` must be `..` (repo root) with `dockerfile: apps/tee-worker/Dockerfile`, not a narrower `apps/tee-worker` context.
The `tee_key_state` table uses columns `current_public_key` (bytea) and `current_epoch` — not `public_key`. Raw SQL queries against it need the bytea→hex cast.
The api-client pre-commit gate (`check-api-client.sh`) only fires when `.entity.ts`/`.dto.ts`/`.controller.ts` changes cause `openapi.json` to diff — internal entity changes don't trigger it.

The plan-checker's own suggested fix values can themselves be wrong — it suggested `@Column returns 6` but the actual retained count was 7 (it missed `userId`). Always read the source before trusting the checker's fix hints.
The running API in this project is typically `node dist/main` (pre-built), not watch mode — any source change requires a full `pnpm build` + process restart before the change takes effect.

code.finding: Security-critical ordering: `verifyIpnsRecordSignature` and `continue` at 108-118 runs before `decryptWithFallback` at 122; binding check uses `deriveEd25519PublicKey(decryptedKey)` vs `publicKeyFromIpnsName` (never `parsed.pubKey`, which is undefined for Ed25519 identity records); `newSequenceNumber: parsed.sequence.toString()` at 173 (no increment); key zeroed on every path (binding-fail 135, success 164, catch 184).
Stale-epoch guard (`ReEnrollRequiredError`) fires at line 86 BEFORE any `decryptIpnsKey`/unwrap call — defense-in-depth means a stale key is never decrypted. Key zeroed in `finally` at line 56.

`renewIpnsRecord` takes no cid or sequence argument — both are sourced exclusively from `parseIpnsRecord(marshaledExistingRecord)`, making it structurally impossible to repoint the CID or increment the sequence number.

TypeORM `innerJoin(IpnsRecord, 'r', ...).take(2000).getMany()` pattern crashes at runtime with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'databaseName')` due to TypeORM metadata resolution failure on the paginated join path. Unit tests with mocked query-builders pass silently; only live e2e reveals this. Fix: use `.find({ relations, where })` FindOptions API instead.
Entity columns are `current_public_key` (bytea) and `current_epoch` — raw SQL queries must use these names and cast bytea to hex via `encode(current_public_key, 'hex')`.

`readTeeKeys()` originally queried a non-existent `public_key` column and omitted the bytea→hex cast; fixed to `encode(current_public_key, 'hex') as public_key`. TypeScript cannot catch wrong SQL column names — e2e suites with raw SQL need manual schema verification against the entity.
Database name defaults to `'cipherbox'` here (not from `.env`) — this is the authoritative source for which DB the running API targets, overriding any stray `DB_DATABASE` in `.env`.

workflow: TypeORM query-builder paths with `innerJoin` + `take` pagination fail at runtime with metadata errors that mocked unit tests never surface — the sdk-e2e live round-trip is the only gate that catches this class of bug.

When running a live e2e suite against a locally started API, `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET` must be set explicitly on the API process to match the e2e harness default (`e2e-test-secret-do-not-use-in-production`), otherwise all account-creation calls return 401.

Migration CLI (`data-source.ts`) resolves `DB_DATABASE` from `.env`, which may differ from the runtime `app.module.ts` default — always force-set `DB_DATABASE` explicitly in migration commands to avoid targeting the wrong database.

For pnpm monorepo phases with worktree fragility, sequential execution on the main installed tree is more reliable than worktree-isolated parallel subagents — reliability over wall-clock speed when `node_modules` and built dists are required.

After building a new tee-worker Docker image, confirm the container's `StartedAt` timestamp is later than the build to ensure the running container reflects the new source; the daemon may be serving a cached older image.

When the API runs as pre-built `node dist/main`, source changes require `pnpm build` + process restart — the running process does not hot-reload; skipping the rebuild step means the live gate tests stale behavior.

The GSD plan-checker is a useful quality gate but its suggested fix values should be verified against the actual source code rather than applied directly — it operates on static analysis and can miscalculate counts.

friction: GSD commit helper false-negative fired 4+ times across the session: returned `commit_failed` on every commit including the final bug-fix commit, requiring manual `git log` verification each time.

Stray `DB_DATABASE=cipherbox_test` in `apps/api/.env` caused the migration CLI to apply to the wrong database, making it appear as if the migration ran while the real `cipherbox` DB was unchanged — required significant debugging to diagnose.

`docker compose exec postgres psql` queries hitting `cipherbox` while the API used `cipherbox_test` created a false contradiction (migration appeared applied but columns still present), consuming several turns to resolve.

The stale tee-worker container (2-3 weeks old, pre-67-06 code) was running on :3002 and was not automatically replaced by 67-05 adding the service to compose — manual `docker compose up -d --build tee-worker` was required.
The stale API (`node dist/main`, pre-67-07) required manual identification, kill, rebuild, and restart with correct env vars — the process was not visible via standard service management.

TypeORM `innerJoin` + `take` pagination crash (`databaseName` undefined) only surfaced during the live e2e, not during unit tests or typecheck — caused Test A to time out with a cryptic error requiring API log inspection.
`readTeeKeys` wrong column name (`public_key` vs `current_public_key`) was undetectable at compile time — only failed at runtime during the live gate.
The plan-checker's suggested `@Column` count fix (6) was itself incorrect — reading `republish-schedule.entity.ts` revealed the true count was 7 (`userId` was missed).
The final bug-fix commit timed out waiting for 1Password biometric approval, leaving the commit status ambiguous and requiring a follow-up `git log` check.
The assistant unnecessarily handed the live migration and e2e gate back to the user as a runbook when it had all the tools and access to drive it directly — required user correction.
open_items: Verify the `getDueEntries` fix + spec realignment + `readTeeKeys` column fix commits actually landed after the 1Password timeout — run `git log --oneline -5` to confirm.

`67-VALIDATION.md` remains a frontmatter-only template draft (intentionally left per §5.5 design); should be populated from `67-RESEARCH.md`'s Validation Architecture table before or during execution monitoring.
